decisions.reason: It won an award and is close to the firm’s core dairy range, so its observed performance likely exceeds aspiration levels and in a growing industry there is little reason to redeploy the resources.

Its prominent placement on the home page suggests encouraging early acceptance, and as an incremental cheese variant it fits existing capabilities and can be retained under moderate organisational slack.

Although the website shows no strong performance signal beyond being listed, it is a close extension of the established cheese business and there is no clear evidence of a shortfall that would trigger dropping it.

This product builds directly on the firm’s existing cheese offer, and with industry turnover rising and no visible signs of strain the firm is more likely to continue testing it than to withdraw it quickly.

The firm explicitly presented this new mild soft cheese as part of its broadened offer, so absent negative feedback management would likely keep it as a core-adjacent extension while results remain uncertain.

It has the weakest public signal beyond website mention, but because it still uses established soft-cheese capabilities and the firm appears to have some slack, withdrawal within a year is possible but still less likely than retention.
